speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked	the Minister for Finance (a) what are the scope and terms of reference of the Future Economy Council; (b) how does the new Council intend to work and coordinate with the other economic agencies and efforts to tackle challenges of the future economy; and (c) what are the desired outcomes set for the Council.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Industries and jobs are changing due to changes in technology, demand patterns and supply conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, digital technology is likely to trigger changes in many industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These changes will bring new opportunities and new challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After extensive consultation, the Committee on the Future Economy (CFE) has proposed a set of recommendations to guide our approach.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The CFE's strategies have set the broad directions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, growing an economy that is vibrant, open and connected to the world, supporting the growth of new and existing industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, strengthening our enterprises through industry-specific transformations to help them grow, innovate and scale up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And third, enabling Singaporeans to acquire and utilise deep skills, so as to seize opportunities in the future economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All these will require close collaboration among the tripartite partners.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government, industries, unions and individuals all have key parts to play.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Council, therefore, comprises representatives from the Government, private sector, unions, Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) and Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the industry level, we have Industry Tripartite Committees leading the work on the ITMs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The work culminated in the Construction Productivity R&D Roadmap, which is being incorporated as part of the Construction ITM.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This example illustrates how different stakeholders can come together, each bringing their unique strengths, to advance the construction industry.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The structural changes that are happening in the global economy will require us to respond robustly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All parties will need to each do our best and work in close partnership to respond to change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, we can build a value-creating economy that is open and connected to the world, offering a multitude of opportunities and creating good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We need to really move fast and move decisively, as these are among the key success factors.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While the establishment of the Steering Council would help the various stakeholders align and better coordinate across the various verticals within the Government, I would like to ask the Minister whether the Council would also help to achieve the agility that the CFE had emphasised on a lot in the report that the Minister had mentioned and whether having a Council such as this would help it to be able to move fast and decisively.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We are happy that many of our suggestions are featured in the CFE report.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I agree with Mr Liang that we need to move fast and decisively, especially given the rapid changes that I mentioned − changes in technology, demand patterns and supply conditions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We need to continuously anticipate and embrace these changes and transform our economy for the future.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the same time, we know that we cannot predict the future with any certainty and, therefore, we will not be able to anticipate every single change and trend.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, we must have the agility to make changes and adjustments along the way and ensure that we continue to be in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In fact, the ITMs that we are working on are not meant to be cast in stone.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Neither are they meant to be a kind of fixed marked paths for us to just follow.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will have to map and remap our paths along the journey.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is not something that the Council alone can do.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The FEC members from the private sector, unions and TACs play an important role in this, not just in the FEC meetings themselves, but also in helping to disseminate the message of the need for change and the agility to change.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We need all stakeholders to come on board this in order for us to be successful.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I would say that, more importantly, the FEC is here to create and enhance the environment for our entrepreneurs and businesses to thrive.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I hope that our entrepreneurs and businesses will continue to move fast, seize opportunities, make use of the Government schemes and facilitation in their growth and internationalisation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As to Mr Liang's second question on suggestions that were made and how we would go about consultation, the GPC for Finance, and Trade and Industry has, indeed, given many valuable ideas and suggestions during the CFE process.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On engagement, the short answer is yes, definitely.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Engagement is a key and vital part of the current phase of our FEC work.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This engagement will continue with focus group discussions, thematic engagement sessions, visits to companies, unions, TACs and IHLs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Earlier on, I shared the example of the engagements done as part of the Construction ITM.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Members can see that with 400-over stakeholders, how much effort went into doing that.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Many engagement sessions with stakeholders have been held and we will continue to hold them.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Similar engagement and consultation efforts are going on in other ITMs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I had spoken of only one ITM but there are many other ITMs for which the work will be continuing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We welcome suggestions on how we can continue to do this even better and strike a good balance between consultation and implementation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One, would the Minister consider under the CFE developing a new literacy curriculum for the 21st century workforce, especially for the adults, so that everyone would be able to rise above the current skills level and be a bit more future-ready?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Three, addressing what I see is a development where, for example, in transport, many of our professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) are taking to becoming Uber and Grab drivers when the development in the future economy is really towards driverless vehicles.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: First, on whether CFE would develop a new literacy curriculum for adults, the skillsets which are needed for all of us as working adults will change and keep changing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: That is why SkillsFuture is such an important part of this effort.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: What we do know is that we do need to equip many of our people with greater skills in information and communications technology (ICT).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I mentioned that ICT is one sector for which many industries will be affected and transformed.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are hoping to use ICT to transform many of these industries and create better jobs for our people.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There will be a lot of new skills that are needed.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Whether it should be something that applies generically across all sectors or whether it should be targeted at particular sectors is a subject that we are studying.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I had several discussions with Minister Lim Swee Say on this matter as well as with Minister Ong Ye Kung and Minister Josephine Teo on skills and specific segments of our workforce that we have to pay special attention to.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have to think about not just the skills but the job redesign that is necessary.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Again, this is something which the tripartite committee will have to look at.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Every of the ITMs will need to address some of these critical issues.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Similarly, the Member's third question on PMETs and how technology will change their jobs, we are fortunate that our educational standards and level and the skills of our people have gone up over the years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are in a better position today to adjust to these changes and we will perform.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But at the same time, the pace of change has also accelerated.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, how do we ensure that all our workers, whether they are PMETs or non-PMETs, continue to have the skills to make changes?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Which are the sectors for which the change will be even more rapid?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I would say that given the pace, the nature of technology, it is difficult to predict that there is one particular area A or B that will be more at risk.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But we will try and, at the same time, we need the industries, we need the companies to work together with us to ensure that these changes are made smoothly.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
